answer.rationale: With only one decision slot and a binding 14-day deadline on a non-auto-renewing contract, the priority is to avoid introducing integration or delivery risk into an already bufferless line. Memory C1 indicates that renewing with the incumbent has twice kept integration stable with no migration work and no interruption to scheduled deliveries. The primary question before committing is whether the incumbent's volume pricing and payment terms can be preserved or improved, since Finance has mandated an 18% cost cut. Memory C6 records that multi-year commitments with the incumbent unlocked volume pricing and cut unit cost without narrowing service scope. If the archived C6 record supports that conclusion, I intend to renew the incumbent contract, negotiating for a multi-year term with volume pricing to meet the cost-cut target while avoiding migration risk at a moment when the assembly line has no buffer. I am downgrading the risk flag on C6 to preserve uncertainty around the incumbent's long-term unit-cost reduction, because current market conditions may have shifted since that experience. Deferral is ruled out because the contract does not auto-renew, and switching primary vendors or adding a second source this cycle would create onboarding risk that the line cannot absorb. Negotiate_terms as a standalone action is not actionable here because the contract expiration is the binding constraint, but the multi-year volume-pricing structure from C6 is the mechanism I intend to fold into the renewal.
